validations.oracle: known-effect confounded simulation and analytical AIPW score identity
validations.rationale: The causal API is evidence-bearing only when nuisance predictions are out of fold and the returned row scores reconstruct an effect known from the simulation. Separate tests cover ATT denominator influence, grouped variance, repeated folds, negative controls, and binary outcomes.

validations.oracle: non-monotone three-group coefficient and fitted-mean identity
validations.rationale: A numeric code column does not acquire indicator expansion merely because classify_columns calls it categorical. The fitted three-group pattern proves autospec selected a group learner rather than one slope.

validations.oracle: declared-order preservation and explicit-loss warning contract
validations.rationale: The current formula path cannot apply ordered numeric learners directly to categorical labels. Keeping a valid group learner is acceptable only when the lost ordering and explicit-score alternatives are visible to the caller.

The effects API retains prediction-scale, population, weights and support. A linear oracle makes the ALE accumulation independently checkable; adjacent tests cover nonidentity-link contrasts, LSS functionals, elasticities, factors, ICE and support refusals.

validations.oracle: full categorical log-loss and multiclass Brier analytical identities
validations.rationale: The shared evaluation result must retain every probability column and stable class identity rather than the upstream partial reported risk. Binary, count, pairing, rolling-fold and fit-budget oracles are covered in the same test module.

Width alone rewards empty intervals. The hand calculation verifies that width and alpha-scaled miss penalties are aggregated with the declared evaluation weights while nominal and empirical coverage remain separate.
The loaded binary, rather than the current checkout, must identify the native code that produced a fit or benchmark. Package version remains a separate release identifier.
A source-tree commit and RUSTFLAGS environment cannot prove which already-built extension was imported. Benchmark artifacts now copy identity from the binary itself.

validations.oracle: analytical Gaussian density, CRPS, PIT, interval-score and exceedance identities
validations.rationale: Distributional evaluation must combine every fitted parameter and retain the evaluation-data role. A separate fixed zero-adjusted Gamma test verifies F(y-) to F(y) randomization at an atom while continuous observations remain seed-invariant.

validations.oracle: nested conditional-quantile ordering and row-identity contract
validations.rationale: A centile fan must preserve the fitted row-specific distributions and state that optional split panels facet one model rather than fit separate groups.

validations.oracle: explicit average of row-specific fitted densities
validations.rationale: Evaluating one density at average parameters is not the marginal predictive distribution when scale or shape varies. The test reconstructs the curve from every fitted row and checks both displayed curves integrate to one.

A probability mass at zero and a density above zero have different units and cannot share one curve. The table and chart keep the atom in a separate panel while both positive-density integrals reconstruct their remaining probability.

An LSS loss is joint across parameters. The profile must localize row contributions without claiming a per-parameter or per-term decomposition, and its bin totals must reconstruct the fitted objective.
A family is useful for growth and reference-curve modeling only when its fitted parameters drive the distributional diagnostics without non-finite values or shape loss.

validations.oracle: analytical mixture and AFT response-mean identities
validations.rationale: The R frontend now exposes the same response-moment semantics as Python. The contract distinguishes component location from mixture mean and refuses parameters for which the requested moment does not exist.

analytical mean log density from fitted LSS parameter predictions
validations.rationale: LSSRegressor inherits location R-squared from RegressorMixin, which cannot score fitted scale or tails. The dedicated scorer is checked against the family density and documented as requiring held-out data for predictive interpretation.

AdaExp minimizes exponential classification loss and does not supply calibrated probabilities. The adapter exposes its signed margin and class boundary while hiding predict_proba; Binomial retains probability output.

SurvivalBoost locates named event and time fields rather than assuming dtype order. Adjacent tests reject non-finite time, route censored LSS families away from numeric LSSRegressor, and accept full or RHS-only formulas.

validations.oracle: typed refusal for an out-of-domain family parameter
validations.rationale: P0.3 asked for the R and Rust artifact readers to be audited separately, since a Python test is not evidence that they reject the same payload. They did not: a hand-edited artifact with tau = 1.5 on a Quantile family was refused in Python and loaded in R, and the model it produced predicted from a check loss minimised below every observation. Eight out-of-domain values across six families are refused now, and two valid documents still load.

validations.oracle: the mboostrs._parity_notes registry, generated into the R package
validations.rationale: P1.4's last bullet: R models did not carry the same first-contact information as Python. There was no parity_notes() in R at all and summary() said nothing, so a difference between a fit and what its name suggests was reachable from one frontend and not the other. The notes are generated from the Python registry rather than copied, since a second prose registry is the failure this project keeps paying for.

The published core crate permitted invalid construction: QuantReg::new/with_qoffset, Huber::new, Cindex::new and PropOdds::new accepted impossible values, and Multinomial::new asserted, so a library call could abort the process. try_* constructors return MboostrsError; the unchecked ones are marked as such; mod checked_construction covers every boundary including non-finite values.

families.name: AUC
families.notes: Weighted case weights are supported via a principled mboostrs extension (see Family::requires_unit_weights == false and the Auc doc comment in families.rs): each observation participates with weight w_i (w_i == 0 excluded), the f/sd(f) standardization is a weighted sample sd over participating observations, and every pairwise term picks up a w_i*w_k factor -- this reduces bit-identically to the unit-weight formulas when w ≡ 1. This intentionally differs from R's own weighted AUC() ngradient, which is broken (returns a compacted vector of length sum(w), not n, an upstream quirk not reproduced here). cvrisk()/stabsel() therefore run for both bootstrap (integer-count) and subsampling ({0,1}) folds, but are only smoke-tested (finite risk, no NaN, a selected mstop, signal-over-noise selection), not R-parity-verified -- there is no R numerical target for the weighted case. predict(type='response') and residuals() use the identity link (the raw ranking score), not a probability -- R's rclass=(f>0)+1 predicted-class rule is not exposed. Information criteria are refused for this family; use cvrisk for stopping selection.

families.name: Gehan
families.known_deviation: Gehan's offset is unidentifiable (the loss depends only on pairwise residual differences, so a constant additive shift of every fitted value cancels and the risk is flat in it); mboostrs defines offset() = 0 rather than reproducing R's arbitrary optimize()-on-a-flat-function value. Gradient, coefficient increments, selected, and risk are unaffected and match R exactly; only the additive constant in fitted differs.
families.notes: Weighted case weights are supported via a principled mboostrs extension (see Family::requires_unit_weights == false and the Gehan doc comment in families.rs), matching AUC's approach: each observation participates with weight w_i (w_i == 0 excluded), W = sum(w) replaces the unweighted n normalizer, and every pairwise indicator sum picks up a w_j factor -- this reduces bit-identically to the unit-weight formulas when w ≡ 1. This intentionally differs from R's own weighted Gehan() ngradient, which is broken the same way AUC's is (a compacted vector of length sum(w), not n, an upstream quirk not reproduced here). cvrisk()/stabsel() therefore run for both bootstrap (integer-count) and subsampling ({0,1}) folds, but are only smoke-tested (finite risk, no NaN, a selected mstop, signal-over-noise selection), not R-parity-verified -- there is no R numerical target for the weighted case. AIC is intentionally unavailable, as for the other survival families. predict(type='response') and residuals() use the identity link (Gehan has no response-scale transform), not a probability or time scale.

learners.name: Bbs
learners.notes: gamboostLSS accepts Bbs and Bols in the same parameter formula; fold-specific smoothing parameters and factorizations are recomputed during CV. R new-data prediction rebuilds a centered basis through the same transform the fit used, so a selected bbs(center=TRUE) term predicts on new data and reproduces fitted() to 1e-15. It refused before, because the bridge rebuilt the raw p-column basis against a fit whose coefficients had p - d entries. The one-dimensional bbs centers by the difference matrix and bspatial by the spectral decomposition of the tensor penalty; using the wrong one runs and is wrong, so mboostrs/tests/test_centered_newdata_prediction.R checks that predicting on the training rows reproduces fitted() rather than merely succeeding.

learners.name: Bconstrained
learners.notes: Caller supplies a non-empty finite constraint matrix C with one column per spline coefficient. gamboostLSS resolves C from the formula environment, recomputes the constrained solver for each weight vector, and supports replay, partial effects, CV, stability selection, and serialization. The iterative solver enforces feasibility approximately; explicit lambda is supported.

learners.name: Bkernel
learners.notes: mboostrs Bkernel is an explicit one-dimensional kernel-ridge learner, not the upstream pathway/GWAS bkernel construction. gamboostLSS recomputes its smoothing parameter and centering for every weight vector and replays new data through the cross-kernel against training observations. It is operationally complete but remains an intentional semantic deviation, so it is excluded from upstream learner-parity claims.

learners.name: Bmono
learners.notes: Shape-constrained P-spline. Available in gamboostLSS with constraint-preserving replay, fold-specific smoothing and constrained solver preparation, CV, stability selection, and serialization. Two inner solvers: the default type="quad.prog" (also R's default) solves the constrained QP exactly and matches R (quadprog::solve.QP via mboost:::solveLSEI) to ~5e-10 for every constraint shape, while type="iterative" is a faster violation-penalty approximation. The approximation leaves a same-signed violation at each boosting step which the path accumulates, so an increasing fit on a falling relation drops 0.675 by mstop 2000; quad.prog holds at zero for every iteration count, which is why it is the default. The R frontend accepts both type= (the mboost spelling) and solver=. Python supports by= for fitting, in-sample replay, and new-data prediction; the R frontend fits a numeric by= as well (mboostrs/tests/test_by_other_learners.R and test_lss_by_parity.R compare it with mboost and gamboostLSS).

learners.name: Bmrf
learners.notes: Available in mboostrs gamboostLSS with fold-specific smoothing, spectral-centering replay, CV, stability selection, and explicit errors for region codes outside K. Python resolves K from env; R resolves K or bnd from the formula environment. Python supports by= for fitting, in-sample replay, and new-data prediction; the R frontend fits a numeric by= as well (mboostrs/tests/test_by_other_learners.R and test_lss_by_parity.R compare it with mboost and gamboostLSS).

learners.name: Bns
learners.notes: Available in mboostrs gamboostLSS with weighted centering, CV, and stability selection. Upstream gamboostLSS 2.1-0 delegates to an mboost bns() constructor that now errors as removed, so this is an explicit mboostrs extension rather than a parity claim.

learners.name: Bols
learners.notes: gamboostLSS accepts Bols and Bbs in the same parameter formula; Python supports by= for fitting, in-sample replay, and new-data prediction; the R frontend fits a numeric or factor by= as well (mboostrs/tests/test_by_parity.R and test_factor_by_parity.R compare it with mboost).

learners.name: Brad
learners.notes: radial basis: Matern(3/2) design against space-filling centres, whitened so a plain ridge penalty applies. Lowers to Buser in Python and to the generic block spec in R, so it needs no engine variant. Centres are chosen by greedy farthest-point selection where mboost uses fields::cover.design, so fits are comparable but not bit-identical to R mboost. Python brad(...) formulas and Brad.design(newdata) use the shared Rust radial basis. Both frontends retain the training geometry for new-location prediction and serialization.

learners.name: Brandom
learners.notes: Available in mboostrs gamboostLSS with weighted preparation, prediction replay, CV, stability selection, and explicit errors for unknown levels. Python supports by= for fitting, in-sample replay, and new-data prediction; the R frontend fits a numeric by= as well (mboostrs/tests/test_by_other_learners.R and test_lss_by_parity.R compare it with mboost and gamboostLSS).

learners.name: Bspatial
learners.notes: Available in mboostrs gamboostLSS with fold-specific smoothing, centered and uncentered tensor-basis replay, two-coordinate partial effects, CV, stability selection, and serialization. Python and R new-data prediction reuse training boundary knots. Python supports by= for fitting, in-sample replay, and new-data prediction; the R frontend fits a numeric by= as well (mboostrs/tests/test_by_other_learners.R and test_lss_by_parity.R compare it with mboost and gamboostLSS).

learners.name: Hinge
learners.notes: Adaptive hinge (kink) learner: one boosting selection adds one hinge at an interior-quantile knot the fit places where the data bends. Each selection stores a ridge-penalized hinge with knot, direction, coefficient and centering (a 4-coefficient vector, hence extract_design is partial). Python replays each selected hinge - applying centre=TRUE centering and the by multiplier - in the in-sample, grouped-newdata and grid-newdata paths, and predicting on the training rows reproduces fitted() to 1e-15. The R frontend accepts hinge() in gamboost and gamboostLSS formulas, rejects factor/character by for the term, and folds by_values at fit and predict.

learners.name: Btree
learners.notes: Decision-stump or shallow-tree learner. gamboostLSS replays variable-length encoded tree increments on row-major new-data designs, supports multi-column trees in Python, and reprepares weighted tree state for CV and stability selection. R currently exposes one predictor per btree formula term.

learners.name: Buser
learners.notes: Caller supplies a finite training design X and conformable square penalty K, matching upstream buser fitting semantics. gamboostLSS preserves original row order and represents CV/stability subsamples only through weights, so the same X is valid for every resample. New-data prediction and partial effects require an explicit matrix keyed by learner name; matrices are never inferred from unrelated columns or silently reused from training data.

learners.name: blackboost
learners.notes: R frontend/algorithm not implemented; Btree learner exists.
